3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

3.2 Festival Safety Manager (Designate: Marcus Tan)
- Reports directly to the Festival Director on all safety matters.
- Oversees the implementation of this policy.
- Chairs the pre-event safety committee meetings.
- Reviews and approves all HIRADC documents.
- Ensures that all incidents and near-misses are investigated and reported appropriately.
- Acts as the primary liaison with SCDF, NEA, and the Police on safety related matters.

3.4 Department Heads (e.g., Stage Manager, Production Manager, Vendor Coordinator, Volunteer Manager)
- Are responsible for the safety of their respective teams.
- Ensure that all personnel under their charge have received the relevant safety briefing.
- Ensure that all work under their control is carried out in accordance with this policy and any applicable PTW.
- Report all incidents, injuries, and near-misses to the Festival Safety Manager.

3.5 All Staff, Contractors, and Volunteers
- Comply with all safety instructions and signage.
- Report any hazard, unsafe condition, or near-miss to their supervisor or the SCC.
- Wear any personal protective equipment (PPE) as specified for their task.
- Do not undertake any task for which they have not been trained or authorised.

4. RISK MANAGEMENT

The Health & Safety Policy header shows latest_approved_version 3.2. Record status: current.

4.1 A comprehensive HIRADC shall be completed for all Festival activities. The HIRADC shall identify hazards, assess the level of risk, and specify control measures. The HIRADC shall be reviewed and updated whenever there is a change in scope, location, or methodology.

4.2 The HIRADC register is maintained by the Festival Safety Manager. Stage-specific HIRADCs shall be prepared by the respective stage production companies and submitted for review at least 14 days prior to the commencement of the build.

4.3 High-risk activities, including but not limited to, working at height, lifting operations, hot works, and electrical works, require a PTW. PTWs are issued by the Festival Safety Manager or a designated Safety Officer. The PTW shall state the specific location, time, and conditions under which the work is permitted.

5. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

5.1 General Alarm
- The general alarm for the Festival is a continuous sounding of the siren system.
- On hearing the alarm, all personnel shall stop work, follow the instructions of the nearest Safety Officer or steward, and proceed to the designated assembly point.
- Assembly points are marked on the site map. The primary assembly point is at the Promontory Lawn. The secondary assembly point is at the Esplanade Park.

5.2 Fire Emergency
- Any person discovering a fire shall raise the alarm by shouting "FIRE" and activating the nearest alarm point.
- Call SCDF at 995. Provide the location of the fire, what is burning, and any known hazards (e.g., LPG cylinders, fuel).
- Do not attempt to extinguish a fire unless it is small and you have been trained to use the fire extinguisher.
- Evacuate the area and proceed to the assembly point.

5.3 Medical Emergency
- All first aid rooms are located at the SCC (Zone A), near Stage 2 (Zone D), and at the main entrance (Zone G).
- For any medical emergency, contact the SCC on channel 1 of the radio network. State "MEDICAL" and give the location and the nature of the injury.
- First aiders are on duty at all times during the Festival operating hours.
- For serious injuries or illnesses, call SCDF Ambulance at 995.

5.4 Bomb Threat / Suspicious Item
- Do not touch or move any suspicious item. Isolate the area and keep people away.
- Report the item immediately to the SCC or the nearest security officer.
- Follow the instructions of the security personnel and the Police.

5.5 Lost Person (Child or Vulnerable Adult)
- Report the incident to the SCC. Provide a description and last known location.
- The SCC will coordinate a search and alert all security and steward teams.
- A broadcast may be made over the public address system in accordance with the safeguarding protocol.
6.5 Safety Officers and First Aiders

Safety Officers are deployed throughout the site during operating hours. They shall
wear a high-visibility vest marked "SAFETY" and carry a radio tuned to channel 1.
Their duties include:
- Monitoring crowd flow and identifying potential overcrowding;
- Checking that fire extinguishers and other safety equipment are in place and
  serviceable;
- Responding to incidents and providing first aid as trained;
- Directing persons to assembly points during an emergency.

6.6 Contractors and Vendors

All contractors and vendors shall comply with this Policy and any instructions
issued by the Safety Manager or a Safety Officer. Prior to commencing any work, the
contractor shall submit a copy of their own safety policy and a risk assessment for
the work to be performed. Contractors shall also ensure that their employees and
subcontractors have received the site safety briefing.

Contractors performing hot work, working at height, or using lifting equipment shall
obtain a PTW before starting work. Failure to comply with this requirement may
result in the work being stopped and the contractor being removed from the site.

6.7 Volunteers

Volunteers are covered by this Policy and shall attend the volunteer safety briefing
before their first shift. Volunteers shall not operate any equipment or machinery
unless they have been specifically trained and authorised. Volunteers shall report
any hazard or incident to their Zone Manager or the nearest Safety Officer.

---

7. TRAINING AND COMPETENCY

7.1 General

All personnel shall receive training appropriate to their role. Training shall be
provided before the start of the Festival and refreshed as needed. Records of
training shall be maintained by the Safety Manager.

7.2 Mandatory Briefings

The following briefings are mandatory for all persons working at the Festival:
- Site Safety Briefing (general);
- Emergency Procedures Briefing (includes evacuation routes, assembly points, and
  alarm signals);
- Manual Handling Briefing (for persons involved in lifting or moving equipment);
- Fire Safety Briefing (includes use of fire extinguishers and fire evacuation
  procedures).

7.3 Role-Specific Training

Additional training shall be provided for the following roles:
- Zone Managers: incident command and communication protocols;
- Safety Officers: first aid, use of the radio network, and incident reporting;
- First Aiders: certified first aid (valid within the last two years);
- Security Personnel: crowd control, suspicious item handling, and lost person
  procedures;
- Stage and Rigging Crew: working at height, rigging safety, and load testing.

7.4 Training Records

The Safety Manager shall keep a register of all training provided, including the
date, the name of the trainer, and the names of attendees. The register shall be
available for inspection by the Festival Director or any relevant authority upon
request.

---

8. RISK ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT

8.1 Risk Register

The Safety Manager shall maintain a Risk Register that identifies all significant
hazards associated with the Festival. Each entry shall include:
- A description of the hazard;
- The likelihood and severity of potential harm;
- The control measures in place;
- The person responsible for implementing the controls;
- A review date.

8.2 Risk Assessment Process

Risk assessments shall be conducted for all activities, including:
- Stage construction and dismantling;
- Crowd management;
- Fireworks and special effects;
- Electrical installations;
- Food preparation and handling;
- Waste management.

Each risk assessment shall be completed using the approved template (Appendix B)
and shall be signed by the Safety Manager and the relevant Zone Manager.

8.3 Review of Risk Assessments

Risk assessments shall be reviewed:
- Before the start of the Festival;
- Whenever there is a significant change to the activity;
- After any incident or near miss;
- At least once every six months.

**9. CONTRACTOR MANAGEMENT**

**10. CROWD SAFETY**

10.1 Crowd density shall be monitored at all entry and exit points, as well as at main stages and high-traffic areas.

10.2 The maximum occupancy for each venue zone is specified in the Site Plan (Appendix A). These limits shall not be exceeded.

10.3 In the event of overcrowding, the following measures shall be taken:
- Zone Managers shall notify the Festival Director and the Security Lead;
- Entry to the affected zone shall be temporarily suspended;
- Additional barriers may be deployed to manage flow;
- Announcements shall be made to direct attendees to less crowded areas.

10.4 All crowd barriers must be properly secured and inspected daily before the venue opens to the public.

10.5 Lost persons, especially children, shall be brought to the designated Lost & Found point at the Information Booth. Security personnel shall follow the lost person procedure outlined in the Security Operations Manual.

---

**11. FOOD AND HYGIENE SAFETY**

11.1 All food vendors shall hold a valid NEA licence and comply with the requirements of the National Environment Agency.

11.2 Food preparation areas shall be set up in accordance with NEA guidelines, including:
- Adequate hand-washing facilities with soap and clean water;
- Proper storage of raw and cooked food;
- Protection of food from contamination by dust, insects, or other sources;
- Maintenance of cold chain for perishable items.

11.3 The Safety Manager or a designated officer shall conduct daily inspections of all food stalls and record the results. Any non-compliance shall be reported to the vendor and the Festival Director immediately.

11.4 Potable water shall be provided for all staff, volunteers, and vendors. Drinking water for the public shall be available at designated water points.

---

**12. ELECTRICAL SAFETY**

12.1 All electrical installations shall be carried out by a licensed electrical worker in accordance with the Electricity Act and related regulations.

12.2 Portable generators shall be placed on stable, level ground and kept clear of combustible materials. Fuel storage shall comply with SCDF requirements.
**13. FIRE SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PROCEDURES**

13.1 The Festival Director shall ensure that a Fire Safety Plan is prepared and submitted to the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) at least 14 days before the first day of the festival. The plan shall include site layout, exit routes, assembly points, and the location of fire-fighting equipment.

13.2 All venue zones shall be equipped with fire extinguishers of the appropriate class and rating. Extinguishers shall be inspected monthly by the Safety Manager or a designated officer, and the inspection date shall be recorded on the inspection tag attached to each unit.

13.3 Fire escape routes and exit doors shall be kept clear of obstruction at all times. Exit signs shall be illuminated and visible, and shall not be blocked by banners, signage, or other decorative materials.

13.4 In the event of a fire or suspected fire:
- The person discovering the fire shall raise the alarm immediately by calling the nearest staff member or using the emergency communication system;
- The Festival Control Room shall be notified without delay;
- Evacuation of the affected zone shall commence in accordance with the Evacuation Plan (Appendix B);
- The SCDF shall be called by the Festival Control Room or the designated Emergency Response Officer;
- No person shall re-enter the affected area until the all-clear is given by the SCDF or the Festival Director.

13.5 Fire drills shall be conducted for all staff and volunteers before the festival opens. A minimum of one full evacuation drill shall be completed on the day before the first public session. Zone Managers shall record attendance and report any absentees to the Safety Manager.

13.6 Hot work, including welding, grinding, or any operation producing sparks or open flames, shall only be undertaken with a valid Hot Work Permit issued by the Safety Manager. A fire extinguisher shall be stationed at the work site, and a fire watch shall be maintained for at least 30 minutes after the work is completed.

13.7 Storage of flammable liquids and gases shall comply with SCDF regulations. Quantities in excess of the permitted limits shall not be kept within the venue. All flammable materials shall be stored in approved containers and cabinets, and shall be clearly labelled.

---

**14. MEDICAL AND FIRST AID**

14.1 A first aid room shall be established at a central location within the venue. The first aid room shall be staffed by registered first aiders at all times when the venue is open to the public.

14.2 The minimum number of first aiders on duty shall be two per 1,000 attendees, or as otherwise specified in the Risk Assessment. At least one first aider shall be assigned to each major stage and to the main entrance.

14.3 First aid kits shall be provided at the following locations:
- Festival Control Room;
- First aid room;
- Each stage manager's position;
- Information Booth;
- Staff rest area.

14.4 All first aid kits shall be checked and restocked daily before the venue opens. The check shall be recorded in the First Aid Kit Checklist maintained by the Safety Manager.

14.5 In the event of a medical emergency:
- The nearest staff member shall render immediate assistance and call the first aid room;
- The Festival Control Room shall be notified so that the emergency services can be summoned if required;
- The patient shall not be moved unless there is immediate danger;
- An incident report shall be completed by the Safety Manager or the designated officer within 24 hours.

14.6 Ambulance access shall be maintained at all times. No vehicles, equipment, or materials shall be parked or placed in the designated ambulance access lanes. The Festival Director shall ensure that the ambulance access routes are marked and kept clear.

---

**15. TRAINING AND BRIEFING**

15.1 All staff, volunteers, and contractors shall complete the following mandatory training before commencing work at the festival:
- General health and safety induction;
- Fire safety and evacuation procedures;
- Crowd management awareness (for staff and volunteers assigned to crowd control duties);
- Food hygiene awareness (for food vendors and their staff, in accordance with NEA requirements).

Version: 2.0 (Current)

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This Crowd Management Plan (CMP) sets out the operational framework for managing crowd flow, capacity, and safety across all public areas and stages at the Bayfront Beats Festival 2025, to be held at The Meadow @ Marina Bay, Singapore, from 15 to 17 August 2025. The plan applies to all security personnel, stewards, venue managers, stage crews, and volunteers engaged for the event.

The plan is prepared in accordance with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) requirements for events with an expected attendance exceeding 5,000 persons, and the National Environment Agency (NEA) guidelines for outdoor events. All personnel must familiarise themselves with this document and the accompanying site maps (Appendix A) before the start of their shift.

2. KEY FIGURES AND CAPACITY
The maximum capacity for the festival site has been reviewed and updated for the 2025 cycle. The Crowd Management Plan maximum_capacity is 12000 persons. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled entry for all capacity calculations, ticketing limits, and safety assessments. No event activity, including staff, vendors, artists, or media, shall cause the total number of persons on site to exceed this limit.

The maximum capacity is derived from the following factors:
- Available open space: 18,500 sqm (includes main lawn, promenade, and food village)
- Seated/standing zones: Main Stage (4,000), Bay Stage (2,500), Discovery Tent (1,200)
- Egress width and exit capacity calculations (see Section 4)
- Fire engine access and ambulance staging requirements

3. ENTRY AND EXIT POINTS
The festival site has one main entry point, one secondary entry point, and four exit points. All entry and exit points are marked on the site map (Appendix A) and will be staffed by security personnel at all times during public hours.

| Point ID | Location | Type | Width (m) | Capacity (persons/min) | Notes |
|----------|----------|------|-----------|------------------------|-------|
| E-01 | North Gate (Main Entry) | Entry/Exit | 6.0 | 120 | Ticket scanning, bag checks |
| E-02 | East Gate (Secondary Entry) | Entry/Exit | 4.0 | 80 | For pre-registered guests, accessible entry |
| X-01 | West Exit | Exit only | 5.0 | 100 | Opens onto promenade |
| X-02 | South Exit | Exit only | 4.0 | 80 | Leads to taxi stand |
| X-03 | South-East Exit | Exit only | 3.5 | 70 | Emergency exit, also used for normal egress |
| X-04 | North-West Exit | Exit only | 3.5 | 70 | Near food village, for crowd relief |

Entry and exit points will be opened at 4:00 PM on Friday and 12:00 PM on Saturday and Sunday. All points will be fully open for exit from 10:00 PM until the site is cleared.

4. CROWD DENSITY MONITORING
Crowd density will be monitored continuously using a combination of CCTV analytics, steward headcounts, and drone surveillance (during daylight hours only). The following density thresholds apply:

- Green (Normal): Up to 2 persons per sqm. Normal operations.
- Amber (Elevated): 2 to 3 persons per sqm. Increase monitoring frequency. Activate additional stewards to key zones. Inform incident commander.
- Red (Critical): Above 3 persons per sqm. Implement crowd dispersal measures, restrict entry at all gates, and activate the public address system with guidance.

Monitoring zones are defined as:
- Zone A: Main Stage viewing area (capacity 4,000)
- Zone B: Bay Stage viewing area (capacity 2,500)
- Zone C: Food village and rest areas (capacity 2,000)
- Zone D: Promenade and walkways (capacity 2,500)
- Zone E: Discovery Tent (capacity 1,200)

Note: The sum of zone capacities exceeds the overall site capacity. This is intentional to allow for movement between zones. The total site count, not zone counts, governs the maximum capacity.
- Additional 6 security officers on standby on Saturday and Sunday, available on call from 2:00 PM.
- Stewards will be deployed in two shifts: 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM and 8:00 PM – 12:00 AM (Saturday/Sunday). Friday shift starts at 4:00 PM.
- All staff must check in at the Ops Room at least 30 minutes before their shift start.
- Uniform and identification badges must be worn at all times.

7. CONTINGENCY PLANS

7.1 Medical Emergency

- First aid posts are located at the Main Stage (Zone A, behind the sound desk) and the Food Village (Zone C).
- In the event of a serious injury, call the Medical Team on Channel 3. An ambulance will be directed to the nearest gate (E-01 or E-02) depending on the location of the incident.
- The ambulance route will be kept clear at all times. Do not block the route with equipment or crowd barriers.

7.2 Lost Child / Lost Person

- Report to the nearest steward or security officer immediately.
- The PA system will be used to make an announcement with a description of the missing person. Do not give out the person's name over the PA.
- A designated Lost & Found point will be set up at the Ops Room.

7.3 Severe Weather (Lightning / Heavy Rain)

- The National Environment Agency (NEA) lightning warning system will be monitored by the Ops Room.
- If a lightning warning is issued, all outdoor stages will suspend performances. The public will be advised to move to sheltered areas (Discovery Tent, Food Village marquee, or the void deck of the nearby HDB block if necessary).
- If heavy rain is forecast, additional stewards will be deployed to covered walkways to manage crowd movement.

7.4 Fire / Gas Leak

- In the event of a fire, the nearest fire alarm point will be activated. The site will be evacuated using the exit points listed in Section 3.
- The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) will be called immediately if the fire cannot be contained with the on-site extinguishers.
- Gas cylinders in the Food Village will be stored in a locked cage at least 5 metres from any cooking area. In the event of a leak, the gas supply will be shut off at the main valve and the area cordoned off.

7.5 Crowd Surge / Crush

- If crowd density reaches Red level (above 3 persons per sqm) in any zone, the following actions will be taken:
  - Restrict entry at all gates.
  - Activate the PA system with instructions to move away from the affected area.
  - Deploy all available stewards to the affected zone to create space and direct the crowd.
  - If the surge continues, the Incident Commander may order a full or partial evacuation.

8. CAPACITY MANAGEMENT REVIEW

As part of the annual review for the 2025 festival cycle, the Crowd Management Plan has been updated to reflect the current site layout and operational requirements. The capacity limits have been reviewed by the Safety Committee and approved by the venue management.

The Crowd Management Plan previous_capacity_limit is 10000 persons. Record status: superseded. This limit was set for the 2023–2024 festival cycles and has been superseded by the current approved limits as stated in Section 2 of this plan. The revision was made to align with the expanded food village area and the addition of the Discovery Tent.

All staff are reminded that the current site capacity limits must not be exceeded at any time. The Ops Room will monitor entry and exit counts continuously, and will stop admitting visitors if the total site count reaches the approved maximum.

9. TRAINING AND BRIEFING

- All security officers and stewards must complete a site-specific briefing before their first shift.
- A full site walkthrough will be conducted at 10:00 AM on Friday, 10 April 2025.
- Refresher training on crowd management and evacuation procedures will be provided to all returning staff.
- New staff must complete the online SCDF Fire Safety Module before the festival.

**Addendum 1: Emergency Evacuation Routes and Communication Protocols**
**Issue Date: 10 April 2025 (Supersedes all previous addenda)**

This addendum forms part of the Crowd Management Plan (CMP) for the 2025 festival cycle. It details the emergency evacuation routes and communication protocols to be used in the event of an incident requiring full or partial site evacuation. This addendum is to be read in conjunction with the main CMP document and the Site Safety Plan.

---

**1. EMERGENCY EVACUATION ROUTES**

The festival site is divided into four evacuation zones. Each zone has a designated primary evacuation route and a secondary route. The routes are designed to move persons away from the hazard and towards the designated Assembly Areas (AAs). The AAs are located outside the festival perimeter fencing.

**Zone A – Main Stage Area**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 1 (North) and proceed along the perimeter path to Assembly Area 1 (AA1), located at the open field next to the car park.
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via Gate 2 (East) and proceed to Assembly Area 2 (AA2), located at the void deck of Block 123.
- **Notes:** The main stage area has the highest density of attendees. Stewards must be positioned at the stage front and along the primary route to prevent bottlenecks.

**Zone B – Food Village and Discovery Tent**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 3 (South) and proceed to Assembly Area 3 (AA3), located at the hard court behind the community club.
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via Gate 4 (West) and proceed to Assembly Area 2 (AA2).
- **Notes:** The food village includes temporary structures and cooking equipment. In the event of a fire, the area must be cleared immediately. The Discovery Tent has a separate internal evacuation plan for performers and staff.

**Zone C – Carnival and Family Area**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 5 (South-East) and proceed to Assembly Area 4 (AA4), located at the bus stop along the main road.
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via the service lane at the rear of the zone and proceed to AA3.
- **Notes:** This zone includes rides and stalls. The ride operators are responsible for securing their equipment and assisting with the evacuation of their immediate area.

**Zone D – Camping and Chill-out Zone**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 6 (North-East) and proceed to Assembly Area 1 (AA1).
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via the emergency gate at the far end of the zone and proceed to AA4.
- **Notes:** This zone is generally lower density, but attendees may have personal belongings. Stewards should remind attendees to leave belongings behind.

**Evacuation Route Summary Table**

| Zone | Primary Gate / Route | Assembly Area | Secondary Gate / Route | Assembly Area |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A – Main Stage | Gate 1 (North) | AA1 | Gate 2 (East) | AA2 |
| B – Food Village & Discovery Tent | Gate 3 (South) | AA3 | Gate 4 (West) | AA2 |
| C – Carnival & Family | Gate 5 (South-East) | AA4 | Service Lane (Rear) | AA3 |
| D – Camping & Chill-out | Gate 6 (North-East) | AA1 | Emergency Gate (Far End) | AA4 |

---

**2. EVACUATION ROUTE ACTIVATION AND CONTROL**

- **Activation:** Only the Incident Commander (IC) or the designated deputy may order a full or partial evacuation. The order will be given via the PA system and the two-way radio network.
- **Gate Control:** On the order to evacuate, the Gate Controllers at the designated gates will switch their signs to "EXIT ONLY" and begin directing persons out of the site. No persons are to be admitted to the site during an evacuation.
- **Route Verification:** The Ops Room will conduct a daily check of the evacuation routes at 09:00 and 18:00 to ensure they are clear of obstructions (e.g., parked vehicles, stacked crates, or waste bins). Any obstruction found must be cleared immediately, and the Ops Room notified.
- **Assembly Area Marshals:** Each AA will have at least two marshals. Their duties are to receive evacuees, provide first aid if required, and report headcounts to the Ops Room via radio. Marshals must carry a high-visibility vest and a whistle.

| **B – Medium Risk** | Services that support event operations but are not directly life-safety critical. | Waste disposal, cleaning services, signage, general logistics, furniture rental. | Medium |
| **C – Low Risk** | Standard goods and services with minimal operational impact. | Office supplies, printing, promotional items. | Low |

The classification of a vendor may be reviewed and updated by the Procurement Manager if the scope of services changes. Vendors must be re-classified if they begin to provide services in a higher-risk category.

---

**4. Vendor Approval Requirements**

All vendors must receive formal approval before being engaged or before any contract or purchase order is issued. The level of approval required is dependent on the vendor category and the contract value.

**4.1 Mandatory Approvals by Category**

The Vendor Management Policy vendor_approval_required includes fire_safety, food_hygiene, and insurance. Record status: current. This means that a vendor cannot be approved for engagement unless they can demonstrate compliance in all three areas.

- **Fire Safety:** Vendors whose operations involve any heat source, cooking, open flames, electrical equipment, or temporary structures must provide a valid Fire Safety Certificate or a letter of no objection from the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) for the specific activity. This also applies to vendors setting up tents, stages, or any temporary structures over a certain size. A copy of the relevant SCDF permit or certificate must be submitted with the vendor application.
- **Food Hygiene:** Vendors handling, preparing, or selling food or beverages must hold a valid licence issued by the National Environment Agency (NEA). The licence must cover the specific type of food operation intended for the event. All food handlers must possess the requisite basic food hygiene certification. A copy of the NEA licence and the food handler certificates must be submitted with the vendor application.
- **Insurance:** All vendors must provide a certificate of insurance evidencing, at a minimum, public liability coverage of SGD 1,000,000 per occurrence. The certificate must name the festival as an additional insured where required by the contract. Insurance must be maintained for the entire duration of the engagement, including any setup and teardown periods. The certificate must be valid for the dates of the event.

Failure to provide any of the above documentation will result in the vendor application being rejected. The Procurement team will not process incomplete applications.

**4.2 Approval Workflow**

1.  **Vendor Application:** The vendor or the engaging department submits a Vendor Application Form (VAF) along with all required supporting documents (e.g., licences, insurance certificates, fire safety permits).
2.  **Vetting and Due Diligence:** The Procurement team reviews the application for completeness and conducts due diligence checks. This may include a review of the vendor's financial health, past performance on other events, and any disciplinary records with relevant authorities.
3.  **Technical Review:** For critical or high-risk vendors, the relevant technical department (e.g., Operations, Safety, or the appointed Safety Coordinator) will review the application to ensure technical compliance.
4.  **Approval:** Based on the category and value, the application is routed for approval as per the table below.
5.  **Notification:** The vendor and the engaging department are notified of the approval decision in writing. An approved vendor is added to the Approved Vendor List (AVL).

**4.3 Approval Authority Matrix**

| Contract Value (SGD) | Category A | Category B | Category C |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **< 5,000** | Procurement Manager | Procurement Manager | Department Head |
| **5,000 – 20,000** | Senior Operations Manager | Procurement Manager | Procurement Manager |
| **> 20,000** | General Manager | Senior Operations Manager | Procurement Manager |
Vendors with a compliance status of "Non-Compliant" in the Vendor Portal will not be awarded new contracts until the outstanding items are resolved. Engaging departments are advised to check the Vendor Portal compliance status of a vendor prior to issuing a purchase order or extending an existing engagement.

**5.3 Performance Metrics and Reporting**

The following metrics are tracked in the Vendor Portal for each approved vendor:

- **Compliance status** – Compliant / Non-Compliant / Pending Review.
- **On-time delivery rate** – calculated over the trailing 12 months.
- **Incident count** – number of safety, hygiene, or conduct incidents reported.
- **Debrief score** – average score from post-event debriefs, on a scale of 1 to 5.
- **Repeat engagement indicator** – whether the vendor has been engaged in more than one festival cycle.

These metrics are used to inform renewal decisions, category reclassification, and the annual review of the Approved Vendor List (AVL).

**5.4 Annual Review of Approved Vendor List**

The AVL is reviewed annually, at least three (3) months before the next festival cycle. The review considers:

- Vendor performance metrics from the Vendor Portal;
- Compliance status and any outstanding corrective actions;
- Changes in business circumstances (e.g., change of ownership, cessation of operations);
- Feedback from engaging departments;
- Changes in regulatory requirements.

Vendors that do not meet the minimum performance or compliance thresholds may be suspended or removed from the AVL. Vendors that have been removed may re-apply in the next application cycle, subject to Section 4 (Vendor Approval).

**6. REMEDIATION AND PENALTIES**

The Vendor Portal vendor_compliance_rate is 0.92. Record status: current.

**6.1 Non-Compliance and Corrective Action**

Where a vendor is found to be non-compliant with any requirement of this Policy, the contract, or applicable law, the following process applies:

1. **Notification:** The Procurement team issues a written Notice of Non-Compliance to the vendor, detailing the specific breach and the required corrective action.
2. **Corrective Action Plan:** The vendor must submit a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) within five (5) working days of the Notice, specifying how the breach will be remedied and the timeline for completion.
3. **Review and Acceptance:** The Procurement team, with input from the engaging department and, where relevant, the Safety Coordinator, reviews and accepts or rejects the CAP. Rejected CAPs must be revised and resubmitted within three (3) working days.
4. **Implementation and Verification:** The vendor implements the CAP. The Procurement team or the engaging department verifies completion and records the outcome in the Vendor Portal.
5. **Escalation:** Failure to submit or implement an acceptable CAP, or repeated non-compliance, may result in suspension or termination of the vendor's engagement and/or removal from the AVL.

**6.2 Penalties and Termination**

The following actions may be taken, in addition to any remedies available under the contract:

- **Written warning** – for minor or first-time breaches.
- **Withholding of payment** – in accordance with the contract terms, for non-performance or non-compliance.
- **Suspension from the AVL** – for a defined period, during which the vendor may not be engaged for any festival activity.
- **Termination of contract** – for material breach, including repeated non-compliance, safety incidents, or failure to maintain required licences or insurance.
- **Removal from the AVL** – for serious or persistent non-compliance, or where the vendor is unable to meet the requirements of this Policy.

The decision to suspend, terminate, or remove a vendor shall be made by the General Manager, upon recommendation of the Procurement Manager, and shall be recorded in the Vendor Portal.

**6.3 Appeals**

A vendor may appeal a decision to suspend, terminate, or remove them from the AVL. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the General Manager within seven (7) working days of the decision. The General Manager's decision on the appeal is final.

**1. PURPOSE**

This Charter defines the sustainability commitments, targets, and measurement methods for the Festival of Lights @ Bay ("the Festival"). It applies to all festival departments, contractors, vendors, and volunteers operating within the festival footprint at Marina Bay, including the floating platform, promenade, and ancillary event spaces.

The Charter is the governing reference for the Festival’s environmental performance. All departmental workplans, vendor contracts, and public communications must align with the commitments herein. Where a conflict exists between this Charter and an operational directive, the more stringent requirement prevails.

---

**2. SCOPE**

The scope covers the full festival lifecycle: planning, construction, event operations, and teardown. It includes, but is not limited to:

- Stage and lighting infrastructure
- Food and beverage (F&B) concessions
- Retail and merchandise
- Waste collection and recycling
- Water and energy consumption
- Staff and volunteer transport
- Marketing materials and giveaways

The Charter does not cover tenant improvements inside permanent structures not under Festival control, nor does it cover the operations of the venue owner outside the licensed event area.

---

**3. GOVERNANCE AND ROLES**

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| Festival Executive Committee | Ultimate approval of targets and budget for sustainability initiatives |
| Head of Sustainability | Charter owner; monitors performance; reports to FEC quarterly |
| Sustainability Working Group | Cross-departmental team; meets bi-monthly; coordinates implementation |
| Vendor & Procurement Lead | Ensures contracts include sustainability clauses; verifies vendor claims |
| Waste Management Coordinator | Manages waste streams, recycling data, and vendor compliance |
| Communications Lead | Ensures public-facing materials reflect Charter commitments |

All department heads are accountable for integrating the Charter into their workplans. The Sustainability Working Group may escalate non-compliance to the FEC.

---

**4. KEY COMMITMENTS**

**4.1. Plastic-Free Target Year**

The Sustainability Charter plastic_free_target_year is 2026. Record status: current. This means that from 1 January 2026, the Festival will not procure, distribute, or permit the sale of single-use plastic items within the festival footprint. This includes, but is not limited to: plastic bags, plastic straws, plastic cutlery, plastic food containers, plastic cups, and plastic bottles.

Exceptions will only be granted for medical necessity or for items required by law (e.g., safety seal on bottled water for VIP areas). All exceptions must be documented and approved by the Head of Sustainability in writing.

**4.2. Waste Reduction**

**4.3. Energy**

- Reduce energy consumption per event day by 20% compared to the 2024 baseline.
- Source 100% of stage power from renewable energy or low-carbon alternatives (e.g., biodiesel, solar hybrid generators).
- All lighting fixtures to be LED or equivalent efficiency.

**4.4. Water**

- Reduce water consumption per attendee by 15% compared to the 2024 baseline.
- All water refill stations to be operational and clearly signposted.

**4.5. Procurement**

- 70% of all new furniture, fixtures, and equipment to be reused, rented, or made from recycled content.
- All printed materials to be on FSC-certified paper or recycled paper.
- All merchandise to be plastic-free and ethically sourced.

---

**5. MEASUREMENT AND REPORTING**

**5.1. Data Collection**

Each department shall submit data to the Sustainability Working Group using the standard templates provided by the Head of Sustainability. Data submission deadlines are:

3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

3.2 Festival Safety Manager (Designate: Marcus Tan)

- Oversees the implementation of this policy.

- Ensure that all work under their control is carried out in accordance with this policy and any applicable PTW.
- Report all incidents, injuries, and near-misses to the Festival Safety Manager.

3.5 All Staff, Contractors, and Volunteers
- Comply with all safety instructions and signage.
- Report any hazard, unsafe condition, or near-miss to their supervisor or the SCC.
- Wear any personal protective equipment (PPE) as specified for their task.
- Do not undertake any task for which they have not been trained or authorised.

4. RISK MANAGEMENT

The Health & Safety Policy header shows latest_approved_version 3.2. Record status: current.

4.1 A comprehensive HIRADC shall be completed for all Festival activities. The HIRADC shall identify hazards, assess the level of risk, and specify control measures. The HIRADC shall be reviewed and updated whenever there is a change in scope, location, or methodology.

4.2 The HIRADC register is maintained by the Festival Safety Manager. Stage-specific HIRADCs shall be prepared by the respective stage production companies and submitted for review at least 14 days prior to the commencement of the build.

4.3 High-risk activities, including but not limited to, working at height, lifting operations, hot works, and electrical works, require a PTW. PTWs are issued by the Festival Safety Manager or a designated Safety Officer. The PTW shall state the specific location, time, and conditions under which the work is permitted.

5. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

5.1 General Alarm
- The general alarm for the Festival is a continuous sounding of the siren system.
- On hearing the alarm, all personnel shall stop work, follow the instructions of the nearest Safety Officer or steward, and proceed to the designated assembly point.
- Assembly points are marked on the site map. The primary assembly point is at the Promontory Lawn. The secondary assembly point is at the Esplanade Park.

5.2 Fire Emergency
- Any person discovering a fire shall raise the alarm by shouting "FIRE" and activating the nearest alarm point.
- Call SCDF at 995. Provide the location of the fire, what is burning, and any known hazards (e.g., LPG cylinders, fuel).
- Do not attempt to extinguish a fire unless it is small and you have been trained to use the fire extinguisher.
- Evacuate the area and proceed to the assembly point.

5.3 Medical Emergency
- All first aid rooms are located at the SCC (Zone A), near Stage 2 (Zone D), and at the main entrance (Zone G).
- For any medical emergency, contact the SCC on channel 1 of the radio network. State "MEDICAL" and give the location and the nature of the injury.
- First aiders are on duty at all times during the Festival operating hours.
- For serious injuries or illnesses, call SCDF Ambulance at 995.

5.4 Bomb Threat / Suspicious Item
- Do not touch or move any suspicious item. Isolate the area and keep people away.
- Report the item immediately to the SCC or the nearest security officer.
- Follow the instructions of the security personnel and the Police.

5.5 Lost Person (Child or Vulnerable Adult)
- Report the incident to the SCC. Provide a description and last known location.
- The SCC will coordinate a search and alert all security and steward teams.
- A broadcast may be made over the public address system in accordance with the safeguarding protocol.

6.5 Safety Officers and First Aiders

Safety Officers are deployed throughout the site during operating hours. They shall
wear a high-visibility vest marked "SAFETY" and carry a radio tuned to channel 1.
Their duties include:
- Monitoring crowd flow and identifying potential overcrowding;
- Checking that fire extinguishers and other safety equipment are in place and
  serviceable;
- Responding to incidents and providing first aid as trained;
- Directing persons to assembly points during an emergency.

6.6 Contractors and Vendors

All contractors and vendors shall comply with this Policy and any instructions
issued by the Safety Manager or a Safety Officer. Prior to commencing any work, the
contractor shall submit a copy of their own safety policy and a risk assessment for
the work to be performed. Contractors shall also ensure that their employees and
subcontractors have received the site safety briefing.

Contractors performing hot work, working at height, or using lifting equipment shall
obtain a PTW before starting work. Failure to comply with this requirement may
result in the work being stopped and the contractor being removed from the site.

6.7 Volunteers

Volunteers are covered by this Policy and shall attend the volunteer safety briefing
before their first shift. Volunteers shall not operate any equipment or machinery
unless they have been specifically trained and authorised. Volunteers shall report
any hazard or incident to their Zone Manager or the nearest Safety Officer.

---

7. TRAINING AND COMPETENCY

7.1 General

All personnel shall receive training appropriate to their role. Training shall be
provided before the start of the Festival and refreshed as needed. Records of
training shall be maintained by the Safety Manager.

7.2 Mandatory Briefings

The following briefings are mandatory for all persons working at the Festival:
- Site Safety Briefing (general);
- Emergency Procedures Briefing (includes evacuation routes, assembly points, and
  alarm signals);
- Manual Handling Briefing (for persons involved in lifting or moving equipment);
- Fire Safety Briefing (includes use of fire extinguishers and fire evacuation
  procedures).

7.3 Role-Specific Training

Additional training shall be provided for the following roles:
- Zone Managers: incident command and communication protocols;
- Safety Officers: first aid, use of the radio network, and incident reporting;
- First Aiders: certified first aid (valid within the last two years);
- Security Personnel: crowd control, suspicious item handling, and lost person
  procedures;
- Stage and Rigging Crew: working at height, rigging safety, and load testing.

7.4 Training Records

The Safety Manager shall keep a register of all training provided, including the
date, the name of the trainer, and the names of attendees. The register shall be
available for inspection by the Festival Director or any relevant authority upon
request.

---

8. RISK ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT

8.1 Risk Register

The Safety Manager shall maintain a Risk Register that identifies all significant
hazards associated with the Festival. Each entry shall include:
- A description of the hazard;
- The likelihood and severity of potential harm;
- The control measures in place;
- The person responsible for implementing the controls;
- A review date.

8.2 Risk Assessment Process

Risk assessments shall be conducted for all activities, including:
- Stage construction and dismantling;
- Crowd management;
- Fireworks and special effects;
- Electrical installations;
- Food preparation and handling;
- Waste management.

Each risk assessment shall be completed using the approved template (Appendix B)
and shall be signed by the Safety Manager and the relevant Zone Manager.

8.3 Review of Risk Assessments

Risk assessments shall be reviewed:
- Before the start of the Festival;
- Whenever there is a significant change to the activity;
- After any incident or near miss;
- At least once every six months.

**9. CONTRACTOR MANAGEMENT**

9.1 All contractors engaged for the Festival shall comply with this Policy and all applicable legal requirements.

9.2 Prior to commencing work, each contractor shall:
- Submit a copy of their Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) policy;
- Provide proof of relevant licences and permits (e.g., for electrical works, rigging, or use of cranes);
- Attend a safety induction conducted by the Safety Manager or a designated Safety Officer;
- Submit a risk assessment for their scope of works using the approved template (Appendix B).

9.3 Contractors working in shared areas shall coordinate with the Zone Manager to ensure that their activities do not create hazards for other workers, volunteers, or the public.

9.4 Any contractor found to be working in an unsafe manner shall be instructed to stop work immediately. The Safety Manager shall record the incident and, where necessary, require the contractor to leave the site.

---

**10. CROWD SAFETY**

10.1 Crowd density shall be monitored at all entry and exit points, as well as at main stages and high-traffic areas.

10.2 The maximum occupancy for each venue zone is specified in the Site Plan (Appendix A). These limits shall not be exceeded.

10.3 In the event of overcrowding, the following measures shall be taken:
- Zone Managers shall notify the Festival Director and the Security Lead;
- Entry to the affected zone shall be temporarily suspended;
- Additional barriers may be deployed to manage flow;
- Announcements shall be made to direct attendees to less crowded areas.

10.4 All crowd barriers must be properly secured and inspected daily before the venue opens to the public.

10.5 Lost persons, especially children, shall be brought to the designated Lost & Found point at the Information Booth. Security personnel shall follow the lost person procedure outlined in the Security Operations Manual.

---

**11. FOOD AND HYGIENE SAFETY**

11.1 All food vendors shall hold a valid NEA licence and comply with the requirements of the National Environment Agency.

11.2 Food preparation areas shall be set up in accordance with NEA guidelines, including:
- Adequate hand-washing facilities with soap and clean water;
- Proper storage of raw and cooked food;
- Protection of food from contamination by dust, insects, or other sources;
- Maintenance of cold chain for perishable items.

11.3 The Safety Manager or a designated officer shall conduct daily inspections of all food stalls and record the results. Any non-compliance shall be reported to the vendor and the Festival Director immediately.

11.4 Potable water shall be provided for all staff, volunteers, and vendors. Drinking water for the public shall be available at designated water points.

---

**12. ELECTRICAL SAFETY**

12.1 All electrical installations shall be carried out by a licensed electrical worker in accordance with the Electricity Act and related regulations.

12.2 Portable generators shall be placed on stable, level ground and kept clear of combustible materials. Fuel storage shall comply with SCDF requirements.

Reviewed by: Priya Nair, Festival Director (signature on file)
Approved by: SCDF FSS (Fire Safety Manager) – Mr. Kelvin Ong

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This Crowd Management Plan (CMP) sets out the operational framework for managing crowd flow, capacity, and safety across all public areas and stages at the Bayfront Beats Festival 2025, to be held at The Meadow @ Marina Bay, Singapore, from 15 to 17 August 2025. The plan applies to all security personnel, stewards, venue managers, stage crews, and volunteers engaged for the event.

The plan is prepared in accordance with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) requirements for events with an expected attendance exceeding 5,000 persons, and the National Environment Agency (NEA) guidelines for outdoor events. All personnel must familiarise themselves with this document and the accompanying site maps (Appendix A) before the start of their shift.

2. KEY FIGURES AND CAPACITY
The maximum capacity for the festival site has been reviewed and updated for the 2025 cycle. The Crowd Management Plan maximum_capacity is 12000 persons. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled entry for all capacity calculations, ticketing limits, and safety assessments. No event activity, including staff, vendors, artists, or media, shall cause the total number of persons on site to exceed this limit.

The maximum capacity is derived from the following factors:
- Available open space: 18,500 sqm (includes main lawn, promenade, and food village)
- Seated/standing zones: Main Stage (4,000), Bay Stage (2,500), Discovery Tent (1,200)
- Egress width and exit capacity calculations (see Section 4)
- Fire engine access and ambulance staging requirements

3. ENTRY AND EXIT POINTS
The festival site has one main entry point, one secondary entry point, and four exit points. All entry and exit points are marked on the site map (Appendix A) and will be staffed by security personnel at all times during public hours.

| Point ID | Location | Type | Width (m) | Capacity (persons/min) | Notes |
|----------|----------|------|-----------|------------------------|-------|
| E-01 | North Gate (Main Entry) | Entry/Exit | 6.0 | 120 | Ticket scanning, bag checks |
| E-02 | East Gate (Secondary Entry) | Entry/Exit | 4.0 | 80 | For pre-registered guests, accessible entry |
| X-01 | West Exit | Exit only | 5.0 | 100 | Opens onto promenade |
| X-02 | South Exit | Exit only | 4.0 | 80 | Leads to taxi stand |
| X-03 | South-East Exit | Exit only | 3.5 | 70 | Emergency exit, also used for normal egress |
| X-04 | North-West Exit | Exit only | 3.5 | 70 | Near food village, for crowd relief |

Entry and exit points will be opened at 4:00 PM on Friday and 12:00 PM on Saturday and Sunday. All points will be fully open for exit from 10:00 PM until the site is cleared.

4. CROWD DENSITY MONITORING
Crowd density will be monitored continuously using a combination of CCTV analytics, steward headcounts, and drone surveillance (during daylight hours only). The following density thresholds apply:

- Green (Normal): Up to 2 persons per sqm. Normal operations.
- Amber (Elevated): 2 to 3 persons per sqm. Increase monitoring frequency. Activate additional stewards to key zones. Inform incident commander.
- Red (Critical): Above 3 persons per sqm. Implement crowd dispersal measures, restrict entry at all gates, and activate the public address system with guidance.

Monitoring zones are defined as:
- Zone A: Main Stage viewing area (capacity 4,000)
- Zone B: Bay Stage viewing area (capacity 2,500)
- Zone C: Food village and rest areas (capacity 2,000)
- Zone D: Promenade and walkways (capacity 2,500)
- Zone E: Discovery Tent (capacity 1,200)

Note: The sum of zone capacities exceeds the overall site capacity. This is intentional to allow for movement between zones. The total site count, not zone counts, governs the maximum capacity.

7.1 Medical Emergency

7.2 Lost Child / Lost Person

- Report to the nearest steward or security officer immediately.
- The PA system will be used to make an announcement with a description of the missing person. Do not give out the person's name over the PA.
- A designated Lost & Found point will be set up at the Ops Room.

7.3 Severe Weather (Lightning / Heavy Rain)

- The National Environment Agency (NEA) lightning warning system will be monitored by the Ops Room.
- If a lightning warning is issued, all outdoor stages will suspend performances. The public will be advised to move to sheltered areas (Discovery Tent, Food Village marquee, or the void deck of the nearby HDB block if necessary).
- If heavy rain is forecast, additional stewards will be deployed to covered walkways to manage crowd movement.

7.4 Fire / Gas Leak

- In the event of a fire, the nearest fire alarm point will be activated. The site will be evacuated using the exit points listed in Section 3.
- The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) will be called immediately if the fire cannot be contained with the on-site extinguishers.
- Gas cylinders in the Food Village will be stored in a locked cage at least 5 metres from any cooking area. In the event of a leak, the gas supply will be shut off at the main valve and the area cordoned off.

7.5 Crowd Surge / Crush

- If crowd density reaches Red level (above 3 persons per sqm) in any zone, the following actions will be taken:
  - Restrict entry at all gates.
  - Activate the PA system with instructions to move away from the affected area.
  - Deploy all available stewards to the affected zone to create space and direct the crowd.

**Crowd Management Plan – 2025 Festival Cycle**
**Addendum 1: Emergency Evacuation Routes and Communication Protocols**
**Issue Date: 10 April 2025 (Supersedes all previous addenda)**

This addendum forms part of the Crowd Management Plan (CMP) for the 2025 festival cycle. It details the emergency evacuation routes and communication protocols to be used in the event of an incident requiring full or partial site evacuation. This addendum is to be read in conjunction with the main CMP document and the Site Safety Plan.

---

**1. EMERGENCY EVACUATION ROUTES**

The festival site is divided into four evacuation zones. Each zone has a designated primary evacuation route and a secondary route. The routes are designed to move persons away from the hazard and towards the designated Assembly Areas (AAs). The AAs are located outside the festival perimeter fencing.

**Zone A – Main Stage Area**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 1 (North) and proceed along the perimeter path to Assembly Area 1 (AA1), located at the open field next to the car park.
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via Gate 2 (East) and proceed to Assembly Area 2 (AA2), located at the void deck of Block 123.
- **Notes:** The main stage area has the highest density of attendees. Stewards must be positioned at the stage front and along the primary route to prevent bottlenecks.

**Zone B – Food Village and Discovery Tent**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 3 (South) and proceed to Assembly Area 3 (AA3), located at the hard court behind the community club.
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via Gate 4 (West) and proceed to Assembly Area 2 (AA2).
- **Notes:** The food village includes temporary structures and cooking equipment. In the event of a fire, the area must be cleared immediately. The Discovery Tent has a separate internal evacuation plan for performers and staff.

**Zone C – Carnival and Family Area**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 5 (South-East) and proceed to Assembly Area 4 (AA4), located at the bus stop along the main road.
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via the service lane at the rear of the zone and proceed to AA3.
- **Notes:** This zone includes rides and stalls. The ride operators are responsible for securing their equipment and assisting with the evacuation of their immediate area.

**Zone D – Camping and Chill-out Zone**
- **Primary Route:** Exit via Gate 6 (North-East) and proceed to Assembly Area 1 (AA1).
- **Secondary Route:** Exit via the emergency gate at the far end of the zone and proceed to AA4.
- **Notes:** This zone is generally lower density, but attendees may have personal belongings. Stewards should remind attendees to leave belongings behind.

**Evacuation Route Summary Table**

| Zone | Primary Gate / Route | Assembly Area | Secondary Gate / Route | Assembly Area |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A – Main Stage | Gate 1 (North) | AA1 | Gate 2 (East) | AA2 |
| B – Food Village & Discovery Tent | Gate 3 (South) | AA3 | Gate 4 (West) | AA2 |
| C – Carnival & Family | Gate 5 (South-East) | AA4 | Service Lane (Rear) | AA3 |
| D – Camping & Chill-out | Gate 6 (North-East) | AA1 | Emergency Gate (Far End) | AA4 |

---

**2. EVACUATION ROUTE ACTIVATION AND CONTROL**

- **Activation:** Only the Incident Commander (IC) or the designated deputy may order a full or partial evacuation. The order will be given via the PA system and the two-way radio network.
- **Gate Control:** On the order to evacuate, the Gate Controllers at the designated gates will switch their signs to "EXIT ONLY" and begin directing persons out of the site. No persons are to be admitted to the site during an evacuation.
- **Route Verification:** The Ops Room will conduct a daily check of the evacuation routes at 09:00 and 18:00 to ensure they are clear of obstructions (e.g., parked vehicles, stacked crates, or waste bins). Any obstruction found must be cleared immediately, and the Ops Room notified.
- **Assembly Area Marshals:** Each AA will have at least two marshals. Their duties are to receive evacuees, provide first aid if required, and report headcounts to the Ops Room via radio. Marshals must carry a high-visibility vest and a whistle.

| Category | Description | Examples | Risk Level |

| **A – Critical/High Risk** | Services that directly impact patron safety, regulatory compliance, or the core delivery of the event. | Fire safety equipment, crowd management, food vendors, electrical installations, medical services. | High |
| **B – Medium Risk** | Services that support event operations but are not directly life-safety critical. | Waste disposal, cleaning services, signage, general logistics, furniture rental. | Medium |
| **C – Low Risk** | Standard goods and services with minimal operational impact. | Office supplies, printing, promotional items. | Low |

The classification of a vendor may be reviewed and updated by the Procurement Manager if the scope of services changes. Vendors must be re-classified if they begin to provide services in a higher-risk category.

---

**4. Vendor Approval Requirements**

All vendors must receive formal approval before being engaged or before any contract or purchase order is issued. The level of approval required is dependent on the vendor category and the contract value.

**4.1 Mandatory Approvals by Category**

The Vendor Management Policy vendor_approval_required includes fire_safety, food_hygiene, and insurance. Record status: current. This means that a vendor cannot be approved for engagement unless they can demonstrate compliance in all three areas.

- **Fire Safety:** Vendors whose operations involve any heat source, cooking, open flames, electrical equipment, or temporary structures must provide a valid Fire Safety Certificate or a letter of no objection from the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) for the specific activity. This also applies to vendors setting up tents, stages, or any temporary structures over a certain size. A copy of the relevant SCDF permit or certificate must be submitted with the vendor application.
- **Food Hygiene:** Vendors handling, preparing, or selling food or beverages must hold a valid licence issued by the National Environment Agency (NEA). The licence must cover the specific type of food operation intended for the event. All food handlers must possess the requisite basic food hygiene certification. A copy of the NEA licence and the food handler certificates must be submitted with the vendor application.
- **Insurance:** All vendors must provide a certificate of insurance evidencing, at a minimum, public liability coverage of SGD 1,000,000 per occurrence. The certificate must name the festival as an additional insured where required by the contract. Insurance must be maintained for the entire duration of the engagement, including any setup and teardown periods. The certificate must be valid for the dates of the event.

Failure to provide any of the above documentation will result in the vendor application being rejected. The Procurement team will not process incomplete applications.

**4.2 Approval Workflow**

1.  **Vendor Application:** The vendor or the engaging department submits a Vendor Application Form (VAF) along with all required supporting documents (e.g., licences, insurance certificates, fire safety permits).
2.  **Vetting and Due Diligence:** The Procurement team reviews the application for completeness and conducts due diligence checks. This may include a review of the vendor's financial health, past performance on other events, and any disciplinary records with relevant authorities.
3.  **Technical Review:** For critical or high-risk vendors, the relevant technical department (e.g., Operations, Safety, or the appointed Safety Coordinator) will review the application to ensure technical compliance.
4.  **Approval:** Based on the category and value, the application is routed for approval as per the table below.
5.  **Notification:** The vendor and the engaging department are notified of the approval decision in writing. An approved vendor is added to the Approved Vendor List (AVL).

**4.3 Approval Authority Matrix**

| Contract Value (SGD) | Category A | Category B | Category C |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **< 5,000** | Procurement Manager | Procurement Manager | Department Head |
| **5,000 – 20,000** | Senior Operations Manager | Procurement Manager | Procurement Manager |
| **> 20,000** | General Manager | Senior Operations Manager | Procurement Manager |

Vendors with a compliance status of "Non-Compliant" in the Vendor Portal will not be awarded new contracts until the outstanding items are resolved. Engaging departments are advised to check the Vendor Portal compliance status of a vendor prior to issuing a purchase order or extending an existing engagement.

**5.3 Performance Metrics and Reporting**

The following metrics are tracked in the Vendor Portal for each approved vendor:

- **Compliance status** – Compliant / Non-Compliant / Pending Review.
- **On-time delivery rate** – calculated over the trailing 12 months.
- **Incident count** – number of safety, hygiene, or conduct incidents reported.
- **Debrief score** – average score from post-event debriefs, on a scale of 1 to 5.
- **Repeat engagement indicator** – whether the vendor has been engaged in more than one festival cycle.

These metrics are used to inform renewal decisions, category reclassification, and the annual review of the Approved Vendor List (AVL).

**5.4 Annual Review of Approved Vendor List**

The AVL is reviewed annually, at least three (3) months before the next festival cycle. The review considers:

- Vendor performance metrics from the Vendor Portal;
- Compliance status and any outstanding corrective actions;
- Changes in business circumstances (e.g., change of ownership, cessation of operations);
- Feedback from engaging departments;
- Changes in regulatory requirements.

Vendors that do not meet the minimum performance or compliance thresholds may be suspended or removed from the AVL. Vendors that have been removed may re-apply in the next application cycle, subject to Section 4 (Vendor Approval).

**6. REMEDIATION AND PENALTIES**

The Vendor Portal vendor_compliance_rate is 0.92. Record status: current.

**6.1 Non-Compliance and Corrective Action**

Where a vendor is found to be non-compliant with any requirement of this Policy, the contract, or applicable law, the following process applies:

1. **Notification:** The Procurement team issues a written Notice of Non-Compliance to the vendor, detailing the specific breach and the required corrective action.
2. **Corrective Action Plan:** The vendor must submit a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) within five (5) working days of the Notice, specifying how the breach will be remedied and the timeline for completion.
3. **Review and Acceptance:** The Procurement team, with input from the engaging department and, where relevant, the Safety Coordinator, reviews and accepts or rejects the CAP. Rejected CAPs must be revised and resubmitted within three (3) working days.
4. **Implementation and Verification:** The vendor implements the CAP. The Procurement team or the engaging department verifies completion and records the outcome in the Vendor Portal.
5. **Escalation:** Failure to submit or implement an acceptable CAP, or repeated non-compliance, may result in suspension or termination of the vendor's engagement and/or removal from the AVL.

**6.2 Penalties and Termination**

The following actions may be taken, in addition to any remedies available under the contract:

- **Written warning** – for minor or first-time breaches.
- **Withholding of payment** – in accordance with the contract terms, for non-performance or non-compliance.
- **Suspension from the AVL** – for a defined period, during which the vendor may not be engaged for any festival activity.
- **Termination of contract** – for material breach, including repeated non-compliance, safety incidents, or failure to maintain required licences or insurance.
- **Removal from the AVL** – for serious or persistent non-compliance, or where the vendor is unable to meet the requirements of this Policy.

The decision to suspend, terminate, or remove a vendor shall be made by the General Manager, upon recommendation of the Procurement Manager, and shall be recorded in the Vendor Portal.

**6.3 Appeals**

A vendor may appeal a decision to suspend, terminate, or remove them from the AVL. The appeal must be submitted in writing to the General Manager within seven (7) working days of the decision. The General Manager's decision on the appeal is final.

**VENDOR MANAGEMENT POLICY**

**Festival Operations Group – Procurement & Vendor Compliance**

**Document No:** FOG-PO-003 (Rev 4.2)
**Effective Date:** 20 May 2025
**Last Reviewed:** 20 May 2025
**Next Scheduled Review:** 20 May 2026
**Owner:** Procurement Manager, Festival Operations Group
**Approved By:** General Manager

---

**1. PURPOSE**

This Policy sets out the framework for the selection, engagement, compliance management, and performance monitoring of all third-party vendors and suppliers engaged by Festival Operations Group ("FOG") for festival production activities. The Policy applies to all vendors supplying goods, services, equipment, catering, security, logistics, and any other contracted support for FOG events, including pre-event build-up, event operations, and post-event teardown.

The objectives of this Policy are to:

- Ensure that all vendors are competent, licensed, insured, and compliant with applicable Singapore laws and regulations.
- Maintain a transparent and consistent procurement process.
- Manage vendor performance and compliance risks across the festival calendar.
- Provide a clear basis for corrective action, suspension, or termination where vendor conduct or performance falls below required standards.

---

**2. SCOPE**

This Policy applies to:

- All FOG employees, volunteers, and contractors involved in vendor selection, management, or supervision.
- All vendors and suppliers engaged for any FOG festival or event, whether on a one-off basis or as part of a recurring engagement.
- All stages of the vendor lifecycle: pre-qualification, selection, contracting, performance monitoring, renewal, and offboarding.

The Policy does not apply to:

- Purchases made through petty cash or corporate procurement cards for minor operational items below $500 per transaction, which are governed by the Finance Manual.
- Engagement of individual contractors for personal services, which is governed by the Human Resources Manual.

---

**3. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **AVL** | Approved Vendor List – the register of vendors who have been pre-qualified and approved for engagement by FOG. |
| **CAP** | Corrective Action Plan – a written plan submitted by a vendor to address identified non-compliance or performance deficiencies. |
| **Compliance Checklist** | The standard checklist used to verify a vendor's licences, insurance, safety records, and other mandatory requirements. |
| **Engaging Department** | The FOG department (e.g., Production, Site Operations, Catering, Security) that requires the goods or services and will supervise the vendor's performance. |
| **FOG** | Festival Operations Group. |
| **NEA** | National Environment Agency. |
| **SCDF** | Singapore Civil Defence Force. |
| **Vendor Portal** | The online system used to store vendor records, compliance documents, and performance assessments. |

---

**4. VENDOR PRE-QUALIFICATION AND APPROVED VENDOR LIST (AVL)**

**4.1 Application and Assessment**

Vendors seeking to be placed on the AVL must submit a Vendor Application Form, together with the following supporting documents:

- Valid business registration (ACRA) and relevant industry licences.
- Certificate of Insurance (COI) evidencing public liability coverage of at least $1 million per occurrence, and any additional coverage required by the contract (e.g., employer's liability, motor insurance).
- Where applicable, NEA food hygiene licence, SCDF fire safety certificates, or other regulatory permits.
- Safety records, including past incident reports and WSH (Workplace Safety and Health) compliance history.
- References from at least two (2) previous clients, where available.
- Any other documents specified in the Vendor Application Form or by the Procurement team.

The Procurement team shall assess the application against the requirements of the relevant engaging department and the nature of the festival activity. The assessment shall be completed within ten (10) working days of receipt of a complete application.

documents.title: Incident Reporting Protocol
documents.content:
CAT-C   Security / Public Order
           – Theft, assault, verbal threat, disorderly conduct,
             lost child, unauthorised access, bomb threat,
             suspicious package, crowd crush or surge.

CAT-D   Safety / Infrastructure
           – Structural failure, trip hazard, electrical fault,
             fall from height, equipment failure, barricade
             collapse, lighting tower issue, water hazard.

CAT-E   Environmental / Sanitation
           – Sewage overflow, rubbish accumulation, pest
             infestation, food hygiene complaint, noise complaint
             (where it affects public safety), weather-related
             damage.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. SEVERITY LEVELS
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each incident is assigned a severity level at the point of first
report. The level may be upgraded (or rarely downgraded) during
investigation. The Duty Manager is the only person authorised to
change a severity level after initial classification, and any
change must be logged in the IRP-F1 remarks.

LEVEL 1   Minor – No injury or negligible injury (e.g., paper
             cut, small spill cleaned on the spot). No external
             agency involvement. Resolved by ground staff.

LEVEL 2   Moderate – Requires medical attention or minor
             repair. Patron or staff may need time off duty.
             Possible media interest. May require NEA or SCDF
             notification if food safety or fire safety is
             involved.

LEVEL 3   Major – Hospitalisation, serious injury, significant
             structural damage, fire, or any incident involving
             police or SCDF attendance. Likely media interest.
             Requires immediate escalation to the Festival
             Director and the Safety Committee Chair.

LEVEL 4   Critical – Fatality, life-threatening injury, mass
             casualty, major fire, or any incident that threatens
             the continuation of the event. Requires activation
             of the Crisis Management Plan and notification of
             the relevant authorities without delay.

The Incident Reporting Protocol reporting_window_hours is 24 hours. Record status: current.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. REPORTING DEADLINES
------------------------------------------------------------------------
All incidents must be reported to the Festival Control Room (FCR)
using the channels in Section 6. The following deadlines apply
from the moment the incident is noticed by any staff member, not
from the moment of occurrence if these differ.

Level 1   Report to FCR immediately (within 15 minutes).
             Submit IRP-F1 by end of shift.

Level 2   Report to FCR immediately (within 15 minutes).
             Submit IRP-F1 within 4 hours.

Level 3   Report to FCR immediately (within 5 minutes) and
             page the Duty Manager. Submit IRP-F1 within 8 hours.

The Incident Reporting Protocol reporting_window_hours is 24 hours;
this is the maximum time allowed between any incident being
noticed and the submission of the completed IRP-F1 to the Safety
Office, regardless of severity level. If the incident occurs at
the end of a shift, the staff member is expected to complete the
form before leaving the site, or to hand over to a named
colleague who will complete it within the window. Extensions are
not granted except by the Head of Safety for operational reasons,
and any extension must be recorded in writing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ESCALATION MATRIX
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The table below shows the default escalation path. If the named
person is unavailable, escalate to the next named person. Do not
skip levels except in a Level 4 situation where you should call
the Festival Director directly.

Incident Type         First Call          Second Call        Third Call
   --------------------- ------------------- ------------------ ----------------
   Medical (CAT-A)       FCR                 Duty Manager       Festival Director
   Fire / Hazmat (CAT-B) FCR + SCDF (995)    Duty Manager       Safety Committee
   Security (CAT-C)      FCR + Police (999)  Duty Manager       Festival Director

documents.title: Sustainability Charter
documents.content:
---

**1. PURPOSE**

This Charter defines the sustainability commitments, targets, and measurement methods for the Festival of Lights @ Bay ("the Festival"). It applies to all festival departments, contractors, vendors, and volunteers operating within the festival footprint at Marina Bay, including the floating platform, promenade, and ancillary event spaces.

The Charter is the governing reference for the Festival’s environmental performance. All departmental workplans, vendor contracts, and public communications must align with the commitments herein. Where a conflict exists between this Charter and an operational directive, the more stringent requirement prevails.

---

**2. SCOPE**

The scope covers the full festival lifecycle: planning, construction, event operations, and teardown. It includes, but is not limited to:

- Stage and lighting infrastructure
- Food and beverage (F&B) concessions
- Retail and merchandise
- Waste collection and recycling
- Water and energy consumption
- Staff and volunteer transport
- Marketing materials and giveaways

The Charter does not cover tenant improvements inside permanent structures not under Festival control, nor does it cover the operations of the venue owner outside the licensed event area.

---

**3. GOVERNANCE AND ROLES**

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| Festival Executive Committee | Ultimate approval of targets and budget for sustainability initiatives |
| Head of Sustainability | Charter owner; monitors performance; reports to FEC quarterly |
| Sustainability Working Group | Cross-departmental team; meets bi-monthly; coordinates implementation |
| Vendor & Procurement Lead | Ensures contracts include sustainability clauses; verifies vendor claims |
| Waste Management Coordinator | Manages waste streams, recycling data, and vendor compliance |
| Communications Lead | Ensures public-facing materials reflect Charter commitments |

All department heads are accountable for integrating the Charter into their workplans. The Sustainability Working Group may escalate non-compliance to the FEC.

---

**4. KEY COMMITMENTS**

**4.1. Plastic-Free Target Year**

The Sustainability Charter plastic_free_target_year is 2026. Record status: current. This means that from 1 January 2026, the Festival will not procure, distribute, or permit the sale of single-use plastic items within the festival footprint. This includes, but is not limited to: plastic bags, plastic straws, plastic cutlery, plastic food containers, plastic cups, and plastic bottles.

Exceptions will only be granted for medical necessity or for items required by law (e.g., safety seal on bottled water for VIP areas). All exceptions must be documented and approved by the Head of Sustainability in writing.

**4.2. Waste Reduction**

**4.3. Energy**

- Reduce energy consumption per event day by 20% compared to the 2024 baseline.
- Source 100% of stage power from renewable energy or low-carbon alternatives (e.g., biodiesel, solar hybrid generators).
- All lighting fixtures to be LED or equivalent efficiency.

**4.4. Water**

- Reduce water consumption per attendee by 15% compared to the 2024 baseline.
- All water refill stations to be operational and clearly signposted.

**4.5. Procurement**

- 70% of all new furniture, fixtures, and equipment to be reused, rented, or made from recycled content.
- All printed materials to be on FSC-certified paper or recycled paper.
- All merchandise to be plastic-free and ethically sourced.

---

**5. MEASUREMENT AND REPORTING**

**5.1. Data Collection**

Each department shall submit data to the Sustainability Working Group using the standard templates provided by the Head of Sustainability. Data submission deadlines are:

- Waste data: within 5 working days after each event day
- Energy and water data: within 7 working days after each event day
- Procurement data: monthly, on the 1st of the following month
- Transport data: within 14 days after festival close

**5.2. Metrics**

| Target | Metric | Data Source |
|--------|--------|-------------|
